predecessors.note: Cliopatria Chalukya Dynasty (Badami) 555-756. The viceroyalty became independent at an undated point after Pulakeshin II fell (the page gives no year).

land.text: Vengi: the Godavari and Krishna river deltas, with the early seat Pishtapura (Pithapuram) and the later seat near Eluru

successors.note: 1077: after the death of Vijayaditya "Kulottunga brought the Vengi province directly under his control" (Kulottunga I page). The Eastern Chalukya infobox gives 1189 and lists the Chola Empire and the Kakatiya dynasty as successors; the line of kings runs on to 1102 on its list but under Kulottunga, who was "first crowned as the lord of Vengi".

capitals.name: Pishtapura (Pithapuram)
capitals.note: The page says the capital was first at Pishtapura, then Vengi, then Rajamahendravaram, and gives no dates for the moves; the span boundaries here are bridging placeholders (confidence 1), not page dates.

capitals.note: Vengi page: "Its capital was at Pedavegi, near Eluru". Dates of the move are not on any page opened; 848 is the reign start of Vijayaditya III, who the Vijayaditya III page calls "the most powerful king of the Vengi kingdom".

correction.text: Vengi: the Godavari and Krishna river deltas, with the early seat Pishtapura (Pithapuram) and the later seat near Eluru

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Eastern Chalukya row). The page gives the founding territory only as "this newly acquired territory" (Vengi, in the eastern Deccan) and the Vengi page as the Godavari and Krishna deltas; no area on the infobox. The Rashtrakutas "overran their kingdom more than once" (undated), so the core was not always held.

union.text: Vengi: the Godavari and Krishna river deltas, with the early seat Pishtapura (Pithapuram) and the later seat near Eluru

correction.text: Vengi plus the Nellore / Kandukur country taken from the Boya-Kottamas

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. From the reign of Vijayaditya III the army "captured the rebel strongholds of Kottama and Nellore" and its general "was made governor of the annexed territory with his headquarters at Kandukur"; the Vengi page puts the limits of Eastern Chalukya influence at Srikakulam in the north and Nellore in the south. Srikakulam is not drawn because no page dates a northern conquest. From 1002 (Saktivarman restored "under the overlordship of the Cholas") the same land is a Chola protectorate: the Chola dossier carries the vassal tint; this shape is the land of the kingdom itself.

region.text: Vengi: the Godavari and Krishna river deltas, with the early seat Pishtapura (Pithapuram) and the later seat near Eluru

ledger.note: 624: Pulakeshin II sets his brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana over newly conquered Vengi. "He appointed his brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana the governor of this newly acquired territory in 624 A.D." The page gives the year and the territory ("Vengi region"), not a boundary; independence from Badami is undated ("possibly" after Pulakeshin II died at Vatapi).

region.text: Nellore and Kandukur, the Boya-Kottama country on the northern border of the Pallava kingdom

ledger.counterpart: Boya-Kottamas (rebel chiefs on the Pallava northern border)
ledger.note: 848: Vijayaditya III opens his reign by taking Nellore. "His reign began with an expedition under his talented general Pandaranga to crush the Boya-Kottamas"; the army "captured the rebel strongholds of Kottama and Nellore" and Pandaranga "was made governor of the annexed territory with his headquarters at Kandukur". The page gives the reign start (848), not the year of the capture.

1006: Satyashraya invades Vengi. "Satyashraya retaliated by invading the Vengi country in 1006 A.D. and placed Saktivarman on the Vengi Throne." The page names Satyashraya only; reading him as the Western Chalukya king is the researcher's.
1006: the page gives the invasion year only; the end of the Western Chalukya hold on Vengi is not dated (Cholas in Vengi under Rajendra later; page silent).
1073: the Kalachuri Yakshakarna invades Vengi. "During this period in 1073, the Vengi kingdom was invaded by the Kalachuri king Yakshakarna of Tripuri."
1073: the page gives the invasion only; no withdrawal date.

region.text: Vengi: the Godavari and Krishna river deltas, with the early seat Pishtapura (Pithapuram) and the later seat near Eluru

ledger.note: 1077: after Vijayaditya's death Kulottunga I takes Vengi under direct Chola rule. "After the death of Vijayaditya in 1077, Kulottunga brought the Vengi province directly under his control." Kulottunga, son of Rajaraja Narendra, had been "first crowned as the lord of Vengi" and ascended the Chola throne in 1070; Vengi had been under Chola overlordship since Saktivarman's restoration "in 1002 CE" (Vengi page).

region.text: Vengi: the Godavari and Krishna river deltas, with the early seat Pishtapura (Pithapuram) and the later seat near Eluru

ledger.note: 1077: the Vengi kingdom ends as a separate state. The infobox of the Eastern Chalukyas page says "Disestablished: 1189" and the lead "until c. 1001 CE"; this dossier follows the Kulottunga I page, which dates the end of separate Vengi government.

wars.name: Vijayaditya III's campaigns
wars.outcome: Vijayaditya III crushed the Boya-Kottamas, took Nellore, "defeated and pursued Krishna II, the successor of Amoghavarsha, till Chedi" and beat the Chedis of Tripuri; the page gives no dated lines.
wars.note: The page dates only the reign (848-892); the Rashtrakuta and Chedi campaigns sit in it without years, and it is silent on Kalinga, Kanchi and the Cholas.

wars.name: Chola intervention in Vengi
wars.outcome: Rajaraja I defeated Jata Choda Bhima, who opposed the Chola-backed Saktivarman; Bhima briefly recaptured Kanchi in 1001; Saktivarman was restored "in 1002 CE under the overlordship of the Cholas".
wars.note: The Rajaraja I page gives no year for the Vengi campaign itself; the Vengi page says late 10th century and 1002. Years here are the two dated points. No border moved: Vengi became a Chola protectorate, recorded in the Chola dossier.

wars.name: Satyashraya's invasion of Vengi
wars.outcome: "Satyashraya retaliated by invading the Vengi country in 1006 A.D. and placed Saktivaiman on the Vengi Throne."
wars.note: Outcome after 1006 not on the page.

wars.name: Kalachuri invasion of Vengi
wars.outcome: Yakshakarna of Tripuri invaded Vengi in 1073; no territorial result on the page.

wars.name: Chola-Western Chalukya war over Vengi
wars.outcome: Vikramaditya VI and the Eastern Ganga king supported Vijayaditya against Kulottunga; "In 1075-76, the war began with the incursion of the Chalukyan forces into the Chola territories"; the page does not name the fighting zone.
wars.note: Vikramaditya VI "could never accept the union of the Chola and Vengi kingdoms under the same ruler".

certainty.note: No treaty lines on any page opened; the delta core is well fixed, the northern and southern limits (Srikakulam, Nellore) are the Vengi page's limits of influence.

notes: Cliopatria has no Eastern Chalukya row (the orchestrator's brief names them as a gap). Five pages, all thin on dates: the Eastern Chalukyas article is silent on every war date and on its own area, so the 848 gain is the only dated expansion and the Rashtrakuta occupations are not dated at all. End year 1077 follows the Kulottunga I page (Vengi under direct Chola control); the infobox says 1189 and the lead says c. 1001, a conflict recorded here, not resolved. The Chola-overlord years (1002-1077) need vassal_start/vassal_end in the chola-empire dossier with counterpart eastern-chalukyas; the 1118-1126 northern loss and 1133 recovery (Kulottunga I page) belong to that dossier. Capital move dates are placeholders. Gazetteer lacks 'Vengi', 'Pithapuram', 'Eluru' and 'Srikakulam' as place names; radii around Rajahmundry, Vijayawada and Nellore stand in. Counterparts needing dossiers: kalachuris-of-tripuri (written in this batch), Boya-Kottamas (no state), Western Chalukya (western-chalukya-empire exists).
